sources.citation: I. G. Gjerde and L. R. Scott, Verification and validation of cylinder drag: Pressure and stress approximations on curved boundaries, arXiv:2306.12362v1 (2023)
facts_used: Eq. (5) displays the Stokes integration-by-parts identity with full traction (nu D(u)-p I)n

Eq. (28) couples that velocity Nitsche form to the volume pressure-divergence form
the manufactured Scott-Vogelius example immediately preceding the Nitsche experiment uses constant pressure

sources.citation: M. Neilan, M. A. Olshanskii, and H. von Wahl, An unfitted divergence-free higher order finite element method for the Stokes problem, arXiv:2512.12050v2 (2026)
facts_used: the abstract identifies loss of pressure robustness associated with weak enforcement of normal velocity
the method introduces a higher-order Lagrange multiplier on the weak boundary
the discrete formulation contains c_h(mu_h,v_h)=integral_Gamma_h mu_h n_h dot v_h
a no-flow experiment with nonconstant pressure is used to probe pressure decoupling
page_images_checked: printed page 1 / abstract and pressure-robustness statement
method section around the boundary multiplier formulation
sources.scope_note: Different unfitted divergence-free Stokes method; used only as independent corroboration of the weak-normal pressure-trace mechanism, not as a proof of the Ridgway prize theorem.
